{{BSE|543711}} | revenue = {{up}} {{INRConvert|608|c|lk=on}} (FY24) | net_income = {{up}} {{INRConvert|93|c}} (FY24){{cite news |title=Sula Vineyards Q4 results: Net profit declines 4.85% to Rs 13.55 crore |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/results/sula-vineyards-q4-results-net-profit-declines-4-85-to-rs-13-55-crore-124050801199_1.html |access-date=8 February 2025 |work=Business Standard |date=8 May 2024}} }} '''Sula Vineyards''' is a [[winery]] and [[vineyard]] located in the [[Nashik]] region of western India, approximately {{convert|180|km}} northeast of [[Mumbai]]. It was founded by [[Rajeev Samant]] in 1999.{{Cite web|title=Sula Vineyards seeks to blend rapid growth with sustainability|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/sula-seeks-to-blend-rapid-growth-with-sustainability/article25655201.ece|access-date=2021-02-02|website=@businessline|date=3 December 2018 |language=en}} Sula has grown to be India's largest and most awarded wine brand. Sula introduced grape varietals such as [[Chenin blanc]], [[Sauvignon blanc]], [[Riesling]] and [[Zinfandel]] in India and is the leading player in the Indian wine industry.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0PHcCQAAQBAJ|title=The Oxford Companion to Wine|last=Harding|first=Julia|date=1 September 2015|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=9780198705383}} == History == Sula Vineyards was founded by [[Rajeev Samant]] in the late 1990s. An alumnus of [[Stanford University]], he worked at [[Oracle Corporation]] in [[California]] after his graduation. After quitting his corporate job, Samant established Sula upon his return to [[India]].{{Cite web|date=13 October 2007|title=Rajeev Samant {{!}} The pursuit of cool – Livemint|url=http://www.livemint.com/Leisure/CuomQL4CzdY6RqU0S6JH7N/Rajeev-Samant--The-pursuit-of-cool.html|access-date=14 January 2016|website=www.livemint.com}} Sula was named after Samant's mother, Sulabha. Samant steadily grew the company over the next few years by introducing newer grape varieties and expanding the company's offerings. Over the last few decades, the Nashik region has transformed and is often referred to as "India’s [[Napa Valley AVA|Napa Valley]]".{{Cite web|title=India's 'Napa Valley': Sula vineyard pioneers eco-friendly wine in an emerging market|url=http://www.theecologist.org/investigations/food_and_farming/1354735/indias_napa_valley_sula_vineyard_pioneers_ecofriendly_wine_in_an_emerging_market.html|access-date=14 January 2016|website=The Ecologist|date=4 May 2012 }} [[File:Wine barrels at Sula Vineyards.jpg|thumb|Wine barrels at Sula Vineyards]] == Wine brands == === Rasa === * Rasa [[Cabernet Sauvignon]] – This red wine is aged in French oak barrels for over a year and then matured in the bottle before release. It contains an ABV of 14%. * Rasa Zinfandel – This rough red wine matures for around 3–4 months in American Oak barrels and contains an ABV of 14%.{{Cite web|last=Blog|first=magicpin|date=2018-08-23|title=10 Of The Best Red Wine In India That Makes Or Break Our Weekends|url=https://medium.com/@magicpin/10-of-the-best-red-wine-in-india-that-makes-or-break-our-weekends-3e87c4f63efe|access-date=2020-09-07|website=Medium|language=en}} [[File:RASA Cabernet Sauvignon.jpg|alt=RASA Cabernet Sauvignon|thumb|RASA Cabernet Sauvignon]] [[File:Dindori Reserve Chardonnay.jpg|alt=Dindori Reserve Chardonnay|thumb|Dindori Reserve Chardonnay]] === Dindori === Sula's Dindori Reserve highlights the winemakers and their endeavours, using their winemaking skills and tools. The Dindori collection by Sula includes three variants: * Dindori Reserve Viognier – This dry white wine has a rich fruity profile and an ABV of 12.5%. * Dindori Reserve Chardonnay – This medium-bodied dry white wine is partly aged in French Oak barrels and contains an ABV of 13%. * Dindori Reserve Shiraz – This full-bodied, dry red wine is barrel-aged in American oak for 10–12 months and contains an ABV of 14%. It is the first ever Indian wine to feature in the Top 100 Wines list by Wine Enthusiast. === The Source === * The Source Grenache Rosé – This rosé wine contains an ABV of 12.5%. * The Source Sauvignon Blanc Reserve – This medium-bodied dry white wine is partly aged in French Oak barrels and contains an ABV of 12.5%. * The Source Cabernet Sauvignon – A well-balanced wine with notes of black fruits. It has an ABV of 13.5%. [[File:Sula Sparkling Shiraz.jpg|alt=Sula Sparkling Shiraz|thumb|Sula Sparkling Shiraz]] === Sula Classics === Sula's wine offering includes over 30 variants:{{Cite news|last=Chandra|first=Alok|date=2011-11-26|title=India's best wines|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/beyond-business/india-s-best-wines-111112600070_1.html|access-date=2020-09-07}} * Sula Brut – matured for 2–4 months. It contains an ABV of 12%. * Sula Brut Tropicale – Sula's first Blanc de Noirs is a blend of 60% Chenin Blanc and 40% includes Shiraz and Riesling. It is bottle-aged for 18 months and contains an ABV of 12%. * Sula Sparkling Shiraz – Sula Sparkling Shiraz is India's first and only sparkling shiraz wine. Matured for 4–5 months in oak barrels, this wine contains an ABV of 13.5%. * Sula Zinfandel Rosé – India's first ever Zinfandel, this wine contains an ABV of 11.5%. * Sula Riesling – This fruity white wine is India's first Riesling and contains an ABV of 11%. * Sula Sauvignon Blanc – India's first ever Sauvignon Blanc, this unbaked white wine contains an ABV of 12.5%. * Sula Chenin Blanc – This semi-dry white wine is India's first ever Chenin Blanc as well as the country's best-selling white wine. It contains an ABV of 12%. * Sula Chenin Blanc Reserve – The limited edition Chenin Blanc Reserve is hand-picked from Sula's Dindori estate vineyards. Partially aged in French oak barrels, it contains an ABV of 12.5%. * Sula Cabernet Shiraz – This medium-bodied red wine is India's best-selling red wine. It contains an ABV of 13.5%.{{Cite web|date=2020-06-24|title=The 10 Finest Indian Red Wines You Need On Your Shelf!|url=https://magicpin.in/blog/10-best-red-wines-india-along-prices/|access-date=2020-09-07|website=magicpin Blog}} * Sula Zinfandel – This medium-bodied red wine contains an ABV of 13.5%. * Sula Late Harvest Chenin Blanc – This [[dessert wine]] by Sula is India's first ever late harvest Chenin Blanc and contains an ABV of 13.5%. * Sula Seco Rosé – This medium-dry rosé [[sparkling wine]] contains an ABV of 10.5%. * Sula Seco – Sula Seco Rose is a medium dry rosé sparkling wine with an ABV of 10.5%. * Sula Satori Tempranillo – "Satori" is a Zen term meaning "sudden enlightenment". This red wine variant is a medium-bodied blend of Tempranillo, Malbec and Merlot. It contains an ABV of 13%. * Sula Brut Crémant De Nashik – a sparkling wine with an ABV of 12%. [[File:Dia Sparkling Red & White Wine Sparkler.jpg|alt=Dia Sparkling Red & White Wine Sparkler|thumb|Dia Sparkling Red & White Wine Sparkler]] === Dia === India's first wine in a can, Dia, was launched in 2019 as a line of wine sparklers. The wine is currently available in Goa and Maharashtra.{{Cite web|title=Sula Vineyards Launches India's First Wine in a Can 'Dia Sparkler'|url=http://bwhotelier.businessworld.in/article/Sula-Vineyards-Launches-India-s-First-Wine-in-a-Can-Dia-Sparkler-/24-02-2020-184832|access-date=2020-09-07|website=BW Hotelier|language=en}} === Kadu === The first Indian wine for a cause: Sula has partnered with Sanctuary Nature Foundation, a non-profit organisation designed to empower and support grassroots conservationists across India.{{Cite news|last=Vishal|first=Anoothi|date=2017-12-15|title=Shiraz with a cause: on Sula Vineyards' Kādu wine|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/life-and-style/food/launch-of-kadu-wines/article21674866.ece|access-date=2020-09-07|issn=0971-751X}}{{Cite web|title=Sula brings India's first wine for a cause to Maharashtra|url=https://www.businesstraveller.com/business-travel/2019/12/12/sula-brings-indias-first-wine-for-a-cause-to-maharashtra/|access-date=2020-09-07|website=Business Traveller|language=en-GB}}{{Cite web|title=FNB News - Kadu, India's first wildlife wine brand, brought to Maharashtra by Sula {{!}} FNB News|url=http://www.fnbnews.com/Top-News/kdu-indias-first-wildlife-wine-brand-brought-to-maharashtra-by-sula-52279|access-date=2020-09-07|website=www.fnbnews.com}} The Kadu collection by Sula includes four variants: * Kadu Chenin Blanc – This refreshing white wine contains an ABV of 12%. * Kadu Cabernet Shiraz – This medium-bodied red wine contains an ABV of 13%. * Kadu Shiraz Rosé – This fruity wine contains an ABV of 12% * Kadu Sauvignon Blanc – This aromatic white wine contains an ABV of 12% [[File:The Tasting Cellar.jpg|thumb|Sula's Tasting Cellar at Nashik]] [[File:Sula barrels.jpg|thumb|Sula's tasting cellar and bottle display at Nashik]] === Sula Selections === Sula also imports and distributes leading international wines and spirits such as Le Grand Noir, Torres, Trapiche, Hardy's, Bouchard Aîné et Fils, Cap Royal, Cono Sur, Gruppo Italiano Vini, Beluga Vodka, Asahi and many more. Sula exports many of its wines to over 30 countries and includes countries like [[Singapore]], [[Australia]], [[Italy]], [[France]] to name a few.{{Cite web|title = Marks & Spencer unveils an Indian wine range – Times of India|url = http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/food/drinks-corner/Marks-Spencer-unveils-an-Indian-wine-range/articleshow/35511656.cms|website = The Times of India|access-date = 14 January 2016}} == Sustainability == Over 50% of all of Sula's energy needs are met by the [[solar panel]]s installed at the winery in [[Nashik district|Nashik]]. The packaging used for Sula's products are 99% recyclable, and the company has planted over 30,000 trees around Nashik in the last few years.{{Cite web|title = Growing green grapes and bottling sustainable wine in India|url = http://www.theecologist.org/how_to_make_a_difference/food_and_gardening/560257/growing_green_grapes_and_bottling_sustainable_wine_in_india.html|website = The Ecologist| date=10 August 2010 |access-date = 14 January 2016}} == Milestones == Sula is considered a pioneer in India winemaking and has achieved many milestones in the last few decades. These are the milestones achieved: * Sula Vineyards was the first company to set up a winery in Nashik in 1999. The company has been instrumental in Nashik earning a reputation of becoming the "Wine Capital of India". * Sula pioneered many classic grape varieties including Sauvignon Blanc and Chenin Blanc in 2000, Zinfandel in 2003, and Riesling in 2008.{{Cite news|last=Balakrishnan|first=Reghu|date=2013-05-16|title=Everstone set to sell stake in Sula Vineyards|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/everstone-set-to-sell-stake-in-sula-vineyards-113051500556_1.html|access-date=2020-09-07}} * Launched India's first Grenache Rosé.{{Cite news|date=2017-11-15|title=Raindrops and rosé at the launch of Grenache Rosé|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/life-and-style/food/raindrops-and-ros-at-the-launch-of-grenache-ros/article20449320.ece|access-date=2020-09-07|issn=0971-751X}} * Launched India's first and only sparkling Shiraz.{{Cite web|last=An|first=Shruti|date=2018-11-05|title=Sula Vineyards Launches Sparkling Shiraz, A Festive Wine Perfect For Celebrations And Gifting|url=https://www.hungryforever.com/sula-vineyards-launches-sparkling-shiraz-a-festive-wine-perfect-for-celebrations-and-gifting/|access-date=2020-09-07|website=HungryForever Food Blog|language=en-US}} * Producer of India's best-selling red wine. * Sula Sommeliers conducted nearly 1300 tastings for consumers and institutions in 2020 * Sula is also one of the few authorised WSET (Wine & Spirit Education Trust) course providers in India. The Wine & Spirit Education Trust often referred to as WSET, is a global organisation that arranges courses and exams in the field of wine and spirits. * Launched India's first "Wildlife Wine", Kadu in four varieties available in Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Goa.{{Cite web|last=Rana|first=Pratishtha|title=Sula Vineyards Launches KĀDU - India's First Wildlife Wine {{!}} Luxebook|date=11 December 2019 |url=https://www.luxebook.in/sula-vineyards-launches-indias-first-wildlife-wine-kadu/|access-date=2020-09-07|language=en-US}} * Launched India's first wine in a can – Dia, in two variants of red and white wine.{{Cite news|title=Sula Vineyards launches country's first canned wine|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/liquor/sula-vineyards-launches-countrys-first-canned-wine/articleshow/74224095.cms?from=mdr|access-date=2020-09-07}} * Sula is the first national wine brand to be listed with TASMAC – the Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation.{{Cite web|last=Balachandar|first=G.|title=Raise a toast! Sula wines to be sold in select Tasmac outlets|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/raise-a-toast-sula-wines-to-be-sold-in-select-tasmac-outlets/article30764651.ece|access-date=2020-09-07|website=@businessline|date=8 February 2020 |language=en}} * Sula's wines are served on India's national carrier, Air India.{{Cite web|date=2014-06-13|title=Sula creates exclusive label for Air India|url=https://www.foodhospitality.in/latest-updates/sula-creates-exclusive-label-for-air-india/6429/|access-date=2020-09-07|website=Express Food Hospitality|language=en-US}} * Sula is the first Indian wine to be listed by Marks & Spencer UK in the year 2013.{{Cite web|date=May 23, 2014|agency=Indo-Asian News Service|title=Marks & Spencer unveils its first Indian wine|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/lifestyle/food/story/marks-spencer-first-indian-wine-jewel-of-nasik-194089-2014-05-23|access-date=2020-09-07|website=India Today|language=en}} ==Wine tourism== [[File:Beyond By Sula.jpg|thumb|Beyond By Sula resort]] [[File:Sula Fest 1.jpg|thumb|SulaFest in February 2020]] Sula also owns and operates two [[Enotourism|wine resorts]] called "The Source at Sula" and "Beyond by Sula" located near its plant in Nashik. It has a [[tasting room]] at its winery in [[Nashik]] and one at "Domaine Sula" vineyard in [[Karnataka]].{{cite news |title=Sula Vineyards Ltd IPO opens today: Here's everything you need to know |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/market/sula-vineyards-ipo-everything-you-need-to-know-8319531/ |access-date=26 February 2023 |work=The Indian Express |date=12 December 2022 |language=en}} Starting from 2008, Sula conducted an annual wine-and-music festival called SulaFest at its vineyard in Nashik.{{cite news |last1=Chandra |first1=Alok |title=A toast to SulaFest |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/beyond-business/a-toast-to-sulafest-116021901007_1.html |access-date=26 February 2023 |work=Business Standard India |date=20 February 2016}}{{cite news |title=SulaFest returns with gourmet music |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/sulafest-returns-with-gourmet-music/article6831012.ece |access-date=26 February 2023 |work=The Hindu Businessline |date=28 January 2015 |language=en}} SulaFest was discontinued after 13 editions, in the aftermath of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite news |title=SulaFest is out but Sula charges ahead with Wine Tourism |url=https://www.indianwineacademy.com/articles/item_4_943/ |access-date=30 April 2024 |work=Indian Wine Academy |date=23 December 2023}} ==References== {{reflist}} [[Category:Wineries of India]] [[Category:Economy of Nashik]] [[Category:Agriculture in Maharashtra]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]
extract: Sula Vineyards is a winery and vineyard located in the Nashik region of western India, approximately 180 kilometres (110 mi) northeast of Mumbai. It was founded by Rajeev Samant in 1999. Sula has grown to be India's largest and most awarded wine brand. Sula introduced grape varietals such as Chenin blanc, Sauvignon blanc, Riesling and Zinfandel in India and is the leading player in the Indian wine industry.
